content:
Hi everyone,

we just opened our first PR (#42002) where we proved the Peano existence theorem for ODEs by using Tonelli approximations.

@Yury G. Kudryashov, maybe this is of interest to you.

We are thankful for any recommendations and feedback.

Thanks!

Neat result, could you split this into some smaller PRs? 600 lines is a bit long to review in one sitting.

Also, could you clarify the amount of AI use? You write "AI was used to help us to adapt our code the style and naming conventions. We also used it in the process of writing a documentation."
So were all of the definitions, theorem statements and proofs done by hand?

Thanks!

Thanks for the fast feedback.

We are not sure, how we could split our result into smaller PRs because of the following reasons:

  1. If we only make a pull request for the Tonelli approximation and some auxiliary lemmas, it is not clear why this is useful on its own at all.
  2. If we push the whole proof, it is easier to decide if our proof of Peano Existence theorem fits to the Mathlib community.

What is the usual amount of lines per PR, given that this is essentially one result in a new file?

We only used AI to adapt our code to the style and naming conventions, i.e. changing variable and statement names, and creating a draft for the documentation of the code. All definitions, theorems, and proofs were done by hand before.

We are happy about any further suggestions!
Thanks!

If you have a chain of PRs, you can absolutely reference the succeeding ones to explain why the current one is necessary. It is quite common. This way a reviewer has the full context where needed, but can focus on just the one at hand. Consider that (without looking at your code specifically at all) a lot of the review suggestions are usually about style in a way that is independent of the broader goal, and this way a lot of the review work can be done independently, and the process moves more quickly. It is not uncommon to have PR 1 be reviewed in detail by Alice (who also takes a quick glance at PR 2), and then PR 2 to be reviewed in detail by Bob. If Alice needs to do both, odds are you will have to wait much longer.

Thanks for the clarification and explanation.

We closed our PR #42002 and opened several new ones:
PR #42142,
PR #42143,
PR #42144,
PR #42146,
PR #42147,
PR #42148.
We tried to split our proof in a meaningful way.

We are happy for any further feedback, thanks!
